hero.headline: JetBlue ending direct flights from Vero Beach to JFK Airport in September
hero.teaser: JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December.
hero.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. JetBlue said in a statement that demand for this new route has not materialized as the airline had hoped.

JetBlue will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route and has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. The route's cancellation comes as a disappointment to local officials and residents who had hoped the direct connection would strengthen ties between the two regions.

The discontinuation of the JFK route after such a short period highlights the challenges smaller regional airports face in sustaining air service to major hubs. While JetBlue's Boston service will continue to provide some connectivity for Vero Beach travelers, the loss of direct access to JFK eliminates what many saw as a crucial link to the New York metropolitan area. The airline has not indicated whether it might reconsider the route in the future or explore other destinations from Vero Beach Regional Airport.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Sheriff ramps up traffic enforcement with 1,162 stops in four weeks
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office is intensifying traffic enforcement this summer, deploying additional deputies and launching a new targeting initiative aimed at reducing speeding and reckless driving across the county. Sheriff Richard Del Toro said traffic is the top concern among residents and described the crackdown as a quality of life issue. Del Toro is using extra deputies from the sheriff's school resource division to boost enforcement while the school year is on break and placing top-performing deputies in areas of concern.

Deputies Christopher Rodrigues and Cheyenne Benning are among those targeting high-problem corridors, including Midway Road, U.S. Highway 1 and Indian River Drive. Benning said the county sees a lot of excessive speeding and that someone recently passed her on I-95 doing 105 mph. Rodrigues said he stopped a driver doing 72 mph on Midway Road and another doing 98 mph on U.S. Highway 1. On Indian River Drive, where the speed limit is 25 mph, Rodrigues said his top speed recorded there was 73 mph.

In the past four weeks, deputies conducted 1,162 traffic stops, wrote 470 citations and issued 1,728 written warnings. The enforcement push is part of a broader strategy Del Toro put in place when he took office. He eliminated the agency's dedicated traffic unit and made traffic enforcement the responsibility of every deputy. Since 2025, the sheriff's office has issued more than 26,000 citations, a 155% increase.

Residents say the problem is hard to miss. Ashley, a St. Lucie County resident, described what she sees on local roads as insane and said nobody slows down. Jessica, another local driver, said drivers are careless and cut people off. Del Toro said he has a family that drives on these roadways and cares about his loved ones and everyone else's loved ones. He said he wants to make the community safer.

cards.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo, Bobby Portis Jr. introduced as Miami Heat players in standing ovation at Kaseya Center
cards.body:
Loud chants of Giannis filled the Kaseya Center Thursday afternoon as the Miami Heat introduced two-time MVP and NBA champion Giannis Antetokounmpo alongside forward Bobby Portis Jr. Heat Head Coach Erik Spoelstra recalled the moment when Pat Riley asked him if he wanted to coach Antetokounmpo, and he said yes. The Greek Freak, who stands 6 feet 11 inches and weighs 240 pounds, said he thrives on pressure and needed to get out of his comfort zone after back-to-back injury-filled seasons. Antetokounmpo told reporters he is not focused on his physical measurables but rather on how many championships he can help bring to Miami.

Antetokounmpo said he feels the Heat route is the best path for him to accomplish his goals. He emphasized that whenever he puts his mind to something, he usually accomplishes it. Riley and Spoelstra said they traded for players who embody the Miami Heat way of play. South Florida has long been known for attracting star players, and Antetokounmpo might be the biggest star yet in terms of physical size. Questions remain about whether the Heat gave up too much for the latest star, especially given his recent injury history.

Portis, who has been playing with Antetokounmpo for six years going on seven, said he prides himself on working every day in the summer to get better. He has been coming off the bench his whole career as a sixth man type of player and plans to bring that aggressive mindset to Miami. Spoelstra said the squad with Antetokounmpo, Portis and Bam Adebayo will play a lot of positionless ball, a style that fans will surely embrace. Portis said his relationship with Adebayo has been built off being competitors, and he looks forward to playing alongside him.

Antetokounmpo told reporters he wants to be coached hard so everyone else will follow his lead. He said he does not want anything sugar-coated and needs the truth so he can apply that to his game. The introduction marked a significant moment for the Heat franchise as they look to add championships to their trophy case. Antetokounmpo received a standing ovation from fans in attendance as he was welcomed to South Florida. The combination of his championship experience and the Heat's established winning culture creates high expectations for the upcoming season.

cards.headline: Donalds, Jolly Lead Florida Governor's Race as Primary Enters Final Stretch
cards.body:
Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly have emerged as frontrunners in Florida's gubernatorial primary race as the August 18 primary approaches. Donalds holds a commanding lead in Republican polling and fundraising, while Jolly has consolidated Democratic support, though both face scrutiny in the closing weeks.

Lt. Gov. Jay Collins used a Thursday campaign call to position himself as the strongest Republican alternative to Donalds, despite trailing significantly in all metrics. Collins defended his support for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and law enforcement, rejected claims of tension between his campaign and staff inside the governor's office, and urged former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner to leave the race. Collins also argued Donalds could struggle in a general election. "This is a two-person race in the primary," Collins said. "It is between Byron Donalds and myself, and we absolutely have a clear path to do this." A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48 percent, followed by Collins at 9 percent, businessman James Fishback at 8 percent and Renner at 4 percent. About 26 percent of respondents remained undecided. Donalds has raised more than $90 million across his campaign operation and holds President Donald Trump's endorsement. Gov. Ron DeSantis, who appointed Collins lieutenant governor in August 2025, has remained publicly neutral in the primary.

Fishback faces dual challenges as his campaign comes under fire. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments. Fishback denies being antisemitic and says the spending shows Republican establishment figures are concerned about his campaign. Collins is also challenging Fishback's candidacy in court, alleging Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassaba. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents. Because ballots have already been printed, the judge said a ruling against Fishback would likely involve directing election officials not to count votes cast for him rather than removing his name from ballots.

Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni. Federal prosecutors allege Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit that managed trust funds for people with disabilities. The indictment alleges the scheme operated from 2009 through 2025. Jolly is not a defendant in the case. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, before entering Congress. Govoni also supported Jolly's past political campaigns and served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S. Senate campaign. In a campaign video, Jolly said he had no knowledge of the alleged theft and welcomed scrutiny of his record. "Unlike too many politicians today who hide behind lawyers or refuse to answer questions, I'm an open book," Jolly said. "Because when you've done nothing wrong, you have nothing to hide."

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway in Martin County after Hurricane Milton tornado damage
cards.body:
Demolition has begun at Murray Middle School in Martin County, marking the start of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage caused by Hurricane Milton. The project includes reconstruction of buildings destroyed in the tornadoes, along with a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a full overhaul of the parking lot. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, though the total project cost has not been finalized. The project is being funded by local capital improvement, sales tax and Public Education Capital Outlay.

Students who were displaced from the affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete. Barriers have already been placed around the work zone to keep students out. The school district said parents can be assured their students will be safe during construction.

"Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," said Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District. "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on."

The district hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027. The tornado damage from Hurricane Milton affected buildings 18, 10, and nine at the school, which allowed the district to incorporate rebuilding those structures into the already planned construction work. The comprehensive project will transform the campus with updated facilities while replacing the buildings lost to the storm.

cards.headline: Florida Fentanyl Summit in Orlando Draws Teens, Grieving Parents and DEA Chief
cards.teaser: Students from anti-drug coalitions across the country joined federal law enforcement at a Florida summit this week to address the ongoing fentanyl crisis.
cards.body:
The Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando this week brought together teens from anti-drug coalitions across the country, grieving parents and federal law enforcement officials. Students traveled to Florida to learn about the resurgence of fentanyl so they can return home with a message about one of the country's deadliest drug threats. Hannah Kahn, 18, and Jasmine Figueroa, 19, are members of their community anti-drug coalitions. Figueroa said she has a relative who is addicted to methamphetamine, and seeing how that has destroyed his life has encouraged her to prevent that from happening to anybody else. Figueroa also emphasized that fentanyl is often not known because it is laced within other drugs that people are seeking.

This year's summit welcomed the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration as a partner. DEA Administrator Terrance Cole spent time with victim families and discussed the ongoing threat. Cole said the poison is being manufactured and distributed out of Mexico by the Mexican cartels. He pointed to new tools from the current administration, noting the president has designated Mexican cartels as foreign terrorists, which opens different avenues for targeting them. Mari Rodriguez's daughter, Imam, died of fentanyl poisoning in 2023. Rodriguez said her daughter made the mistake of buying a Percocet pill that had fentanyl in it, and it took her life. Rodriguez said the fight should have started in 2009, when the first fentanyl was found on streets. Kahn said many people have the stereotype that Narcan is only for responders and EMS, but it should be thought of as a household product, just like Benadryl.

cards.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway after Hurricane Milton tornado damage in Martin County
cards.body:
Demolition has begun at Murray Middle School in Martin County as part of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage from Hurricane Milton. The project will rebuild buildings destroyed by the tornadoes and add a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a complete parking lot overhaul. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, with the total project cost not yet finalized. Funding comes from local capital improvement, sales tax, and Public Education Capital Outlay.

Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, explained the school was already scheduled for significant construction work when the hurricane struck. "Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," said Gernaine. "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on." The tornado damage led to the destruction of three buildings that have now been incorporated into the planned renovation project.

Students displaced from affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete. The school district has implemented safety measures to protect students during the ongoing construction work. Barriers have been placed around the work zone to keep students away from construction areas. School officials have assured parents that students will remain safe throughout the renovation period despite the active construction on campus.

The Martin County School District hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027. The project represents a significant investment in rebuilding and modernizing the middle school campus following the hurricane damage. The reconstruction effort combines previously scheduled improvements with necessary repairs from the tornado destruction, allowing the district to comprehensively update the campus facilities in one extended construction project.

hero.headline: Humane Society of the Treasure Coast seeks fosters, adopters during shelter renovation
hero.teaser: The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation.
hero.body:
The Humane Society of the Treasure Coast is calling on the community to foster or adopt animals as the organization enters phase two of a major facility renovation. The construction will modernize the shelter, improve animal living spaces, enhance adoption areas, and create more comfortable and visible spaces to care for animals. The renovation presents significant challenges for the animals, who are being held in smaller spaces during the work.

Sarah Fisher of the Humane Society of the Treasure Coast said the animals are really being affected by the sound of the construction. It's very, very loud and the sound being in a closed kennel can be very stressful for an animal. About 50 animals are currently in foster care, but the shelter is hoping to get the remaining 67 animals housed on-site either fostered or adopted, with most of them being dogs. The shelter continues to receive animals daily and is on a mission to get them out as quickly as they come in.

cards.headline: Security First Insurance lowers Florida homeowners rates by 5.6 percent
cards.teaser: Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6 percent, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years.
cards.body:
Security First Insurance is lowering homeowners insurance rates by an average of 5.6%, the latest in a series of rate decreases the Florida-based company has made over the last two years. Melissa Burt DeVriese, president of Security First, said their customers are seeing the impact of the rate decreases. Insurance companies have been reducing rates or holding them stable as more companies cite a reduction in lawsuits from state reforms. Burt DeVriese said all those savings they are required to pass along to customers, and they have been. Security First also announced new discounts and a disappearing deductible that rewards claims-free customers by reducing their deductible over time. Over the course of five years, every year the deductible goes down 20 percent as long as customers do not have a loss. Once they have a loss, the discounted deductible applies, and then it resets back to the full deductible amount, rewarding consumers who do not have losses.

Based in Ormond Beach, Security First has about 155,000 policies in the state. Burt DeVriese said Security First is committed to writing more policies in southeast Florida. Premiums in South Florida generally run high, and online firm Insurify reports that in 2026 Florida homeowners pay the highest average premium in the country at $8,292. State insurance regulators said that with more companies and more competition, homeowners should seek better premiums by shopping around.

cards.headline: Florida Panthers to open 2026-27 season against Stanley Cup Champion Carolina Hurricanes
cards.teaser: The Florida Panthers will begin their regular season on the road with four Western Conference games, opening against the 2026 Stanley Cup Champion Carolina Hurricanes on Sept. 29.
cards.body:
The Florida Panthers will open their 2026-27 NHL regular season campaign on the road against the 2026 Stanley Cup Champion Carolina Hurricanes on Sept. 29. The road trip continues with a stop in San Jose on Oct. 6. After the four-game road swing against Western Conference opponents, the Panthers will return to South Florida for their home opener on Saturday, Oct. when they welcome the Minnesota Wild to Amerant Bank Arena.

December will be particularly busy with seven home games, including four special holiday matchups to close out 2026. The schedule includes a game against the Buffalo Sabres on Dec. Fans will enjoy two consecutive five-game homestands, with the first running Dec. 19-30 and the second from March 2-12.

cards.headline: Four Panthers Finnish players make Lantana Finland House a hockey hotspot
cards.teaser: The Finland Club in Lantana on Finlandia Boulevard has become a celebration center for fans of Panthers Finnish stars Aleksander Barkov, Anton Lundell, Niko Mikkola and Eetu Luostarinen.
cards.body:
In Lantana, a Finnish flag waves outside Suomi Talo, which means Finland House in Finnish. Located on Finlandia Boulevard, the Finland Club has been celebrating Finnish culture in Palm Beach County for 80 years. Inside, walls are lined with pictures and crests representing every town and city across Finland. Longtime members explained that Finns came with Flagler, building The Breakers, and then shipped back to Lake Worth in the evenings.

The Panthers roster boasts four Finnish players who have become local heroes: Captain Aleksander Barkov, Anton Lundell, Niko Mikkola and Eetu Luostarinen. All four played crucial roles in the Panthers' two Stanley Cup championships. Last June when Barkov and Lundell captured gold for Finland at the World Hockey Championship, the Finland Club called all the Finns Sunday morning and the whole place was packed. Club member Jorma Olsson said when Lundell scored the overtime goal, the president was afraid they were going to lose the roof. Olsson said all four players are humble, show excellent behavior, and are fantastic representatives of Finland. Last season, 43 Finnish players competed in the NHL. The Panthers hold an annual Finnish Heritage Night at Amerant Bank Arena, with fans flying from Finland to attend in previous years.

cards.headline: Flip City Gym and Cheer gymnasts finish top 15 at AAU Nationals, qualify for Junior Olympics
cards.teaser: Three gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer secured a top 15 finish at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and qualified for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month.
cards.body:
Three young gymnasts from Flip City Gym and Cheer competed at AAU Nationals in Knoxville, Tennessee last month and secured a top 15 finish. Skylar Rose-Daris, Victoria Supan, and Charli Rine competed as one unit after finding their way to gymnastics through different paths. Head Coach Candice Lazuka said the team had a really good season, competing locally, traveling, and advancing to states and regionals. At nationals, the gymnasts came close to a perfect score, earning a 9.9. Lazuka said it is hard to get a perfect 10.

The finish qualified the team for the Junior Olympics in Iowa next month. Rose-Daris said it is going to be really fun going to an entire different part of the world. Supan said the qualification is happy and exciting at the same time. Rine said she is focused on getting first place on floors heading into the Junior Olympics.

cards.headline: Argentina scores late to beat England 2-1, advances to World Cup final against Spain
cards.teaser: Argentina rallied from trailing 1-0 in the 85th minute to defeat England 2-1 Wednesday with goals from Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez, advancing to the World Cup final against Spain on Sunday.
cards.body:
Argentina rallied from behind to defeat England 2-1 on Wednesday, scoring twice in the final minutes after trailing 1-0 going into the 85th minute. Messi fed the ball to Enzo Fernandez, who swept in the equalizer from outside the box in the 85th minute. Two minutes into stoppage time, Messi sent in a cross for substitute Lautaro Martinez to head in the winner. Martinez said he dreamed it and told Alexis Mac Allister that he was going to come on and win it. At the final whistle, Messi fell to his knees in celebration while England players collapsed in disbelief. England had taken the lead in the 55th minute when Anthony Gordon scored the opening goal.

The defending champions will take on European champion Spain in the final on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. England captain Harry Kane said he was gutted for the team, the staff and the fans after working so hard to be there. The loss marks the third time England has come up short in the World Cup semifinals, following losses to Germany in 1990 and Croatia in 2018. Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni said the team showed the collectiveness, the brotherhood, and the fight to the very end, proving themselves after England scored.

cards.headline: Spain defeats France 2-0 to reach first World Cup final since 2010
cards.teaser: Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot and Pedro Porro added another goal as Spain defeated France 2-0 Tuesday to advance to its first World Cup final since winning in 2010.
cards.body:
Mikel Oyarzabal scored from the penalty spot after a play by teenager Lamine Yamal, Pedro Porro added another goal and Spain advanced to its first World Cup final since winning in 2010 with a 2-0 victory over France on Tuesday. Oyarzabal's penalty kick in the 22nd minute came after Yamal drew a foul when kicked by defender Lucas Digne. After a poor first touch with his head, Digne was trying to clear the ball when Yamal raced in from behind to challenge in the penalty area. The ball hit off the elbow of the leaping teen before he was kicked by Digne, playing in his 63rd game for France only six days before his 33rd birthday. Oyarzabal's fifth goal of this year's World Cup marked the first time either team has trailed in their seven games in this tournament.

Porro's give-and-go with Dani Olmo in the 58th minute put Spain up 2-0. A day after his 19th birthday, Yamal was denied a goal on a close offside call that came soon after Porro's goal. Spain will face either defending champion Argentina or England on Sunday in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Kylian Mbappé and France, FIFA's top-ranked team, were trying to become only the third team to reach three consecutive World Cup finals. This win marked the third summer in a row that Spain beat France in a tournament semifinal match.

cards.headline: Photograph of Lionel Messi bathing baby Lamine Yamal surfaces before World Cup final
cards.teaser: Photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 of a teenage Lionel Messi bathing infant Lamine Yamal in a plastic bathtub for a charity calendar, nearly two decades before they face off in Sunday's World Cup final.
cards.body:
Barcelona photographer Joan Monfort took photos in 2007 as part of a charity calendar produced by local newspaper Sport and UNICEF showing a teenage Lionel Messi bathing a baby boy in a plastic bathtub. That baby was Lamine Yamal, who will face Messi's Argentina in Sunday's World Cup final. Monfort, who works as a freelance photojournalist for the Associated Press, told the AP from his home in Barcelona on Friday that he is beginning to have his doubts about whether anything is destined to occur, saying this is beyond all reasonable explanations. The longhaired Messi appears in the images with his hands covered in soap suds.

Yamal's mother won a raffle of families in the city of Mataró, near Barcelona, who wanted to participate in the charity calendar shoot. The 19-year-old Yamal will face the 39-year-old Messi, who is 20 years his senior. Monfort had no recollection of the photos until Yamal's father posted one on social media during the 2024 European Championship. Interest in his photos has skyrocketed with the World Cup final approaching. Monfort, 58, said his heart is split between wanting Messi or Yamal to win, calling Messi the best player of all time while saying Yamal has broken the mold and represents a new, diverse Spain thanks to his parents from Morocco and Equatorial Guinea.

hero.headline: Downtown Delray Beach launches Wellness Pass with free fitness classes and spa deals
hero.teaser: The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August, allowing users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses.
hero.body:
Downtown Delray Beach is encouraging residents and visitors to prioritize health and self-care this summer through a new Wellness Pass featuring free fitness classes, yoga sessions, spa discounts and wellness-focused offers across the city's downtown district. The Delray Beach Downtown Development Authority launched the Downtown Delray Wellness Pass for July and August. According to the DDA, the mobile-exclusive pass allows users to access complimentary classes, discounted wellness treatments and promotions from participating businesses throughout Downtown Delray Beach.

The pass does not require an app download. Miller Physical Therapy is also participating with wellness-related services and promotions. The program arrives as wellness tourism and fitness-focused experiences continue to grow in popularity across South Florida. Many consumers are seeking affordable ways to stay active, reduce stress and support local businesses during the summer months. More information and a complete list of participating offers can be found on the Downtown Delray Beach Authority website.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County Food Bank serves 2,500 daily meals to children at 35 summer sites
cards.teaser: The Palm Beach County Food Bank in Lake Worth Beach supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County, serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children while school is out for the summer.
cards.body:
The nonprofit organization said it supports more than 35 Summer BreakSpot sites across Palm Beach County, serving approximately 2,500 hot meals each day to nearly 1,250 children while school is out for the summer. According to the Palm Beach County Food Bank, the organization prepared more than 36,000 hot meals in June alone. The Summer BreakSpot program provides free meals to children and teens 18 and younger during the summer when school cafeterias are closed.

During a live broadcast on WPTV, Palm Beach County Food Bank CEO Jamie Kendall and Culinary Director Chef Doug Barg gave viewers a behind-the-scenes look inside the Michelle Hagerty Community Kitchen, where meals are prepared and loaded onto trucks for early morning deliveries across the county. Chef Doug Barg walked viewers through the food production process, showing how culinary teams prepare, package and organize meals before they are loaded onto delivery trucks.

Food Bank leaders said the organization continues seeking volunteers, donations and community partnerships to support its mission of reducing childhood hunger in Palm Beach County. Families looking for Summer BreakSpot meal locations can find participating sites throughout the county during the summer months. The Palm Beach County Food Bank is located at 701 Boutwell Road, Suite A-1, in Lake Worth Beach.

cards.headline: Boca Raton TLC Program offers summer volunteer opportunities for South Florida families
cards.teaser: The TLC Program at B'nai Torah Congregation provides hands-on service projects ranging from food support and shoe donations to pantry stocking, literacy efforts and care for seniors.
cards.body:
The program, led by Summer Faerman, is part of B'nai Torah Congregation's broader effort to connect people of all ages with mitzvah opportunities or meaningful good deeds. Organizers say the TLC Program stands for Tzedakah, Learning and Chesed and has helped make service a central part of synagogue life since 2012. B'nai Torah Congregation describes the TLC Program as a way for individuals and families to put Jewish values into action while helping people in need across South Florida. The congregation says the program focuses on hunger, homelessness, literacy, elder care, vulnerable populations, special needs and other community concerns.

Participants can volunteer in a variety of ways, including making sandwiches, serving meals, collecting and cleaning shoes, stocking Little Free Pantries, preparing backpacks for back-to-school efforts, creating Bags of Hope and helping seniors with technology. Organizers say the projects are open to everyone in the community, not only members of B'nai Torah Congregation. Organizers plan to demonstrate volunteer projects such as wrapping presents, making flower arrangements, preparing sandwiches, collecting shoes and assembling supplies for people in need. B'nai Torah Congregation says the program is built around the idea that small acts of service can strengthen the larger community. More information about the TLC Program is available through B'nai Torah Congregation's website.

cards.headline: Palm Beach Zoo extends Kids Free summer promotion through August 10
cards.teaser: Palm Beach Zoo has extended its popular Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10, allowing up to four children ages 3 to 12 to receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket.
cards.body:
The Palm Beach Zoo has extended its popular Kids Free promotion through Aug. 10, giving South Florida families additional time to enjoy discounted summer visits. Under the program, up to four children ages 3 to 12 receive free admission with the purchase of one adult ticket. Amanda Joiner, the zoo's chief marketing and technology officer, shared the updates during WPTV's "Shining A Light" segment from the zoo Monday morning. Joiner said the extension is designed to help local families enjoy affordable outings during the hottest stretch of summer while still supporting the zoo's conservation mission. Zoo officials emphasized that families still receive the full zoo experience through the promotion, including access to exhibits, shaded walkways and animal encounters. The zoo is also encouraging visitors to stay cool with indoor spaces, shaded pathways and frozen treats available throughout the park.

The zoo also announced that its koala joey is officially a boy and now has a name: Bonza. Joiner said that's Aussie slang for awesome or excellent. Zoo staff members from departments ranging from accounting to marketing helped document and share the koala family's journey with the public, according to officials. Palm Beach Zoo also announced the return of its Wild Night Out series, an adults-only after-hours experience happening on the last Saturdays of July, August and September. The themed nights include Paws & Santa Claus in July, Tails & Touchdowns in August and Decades After Dark in September. The events will feature live entertainment, themed activities and performances from bands including Whiskey Six and Snapback. July's event will also serve as an early preview of this year's Zoo Lights celebration. Palm Beach Zoo is located at 1301 Summit Blvd.

hero.headline: Donalds, Jolly Lead Florida Governor's Race as Primary Enters Final Stretch
hero.body:
Republican U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly have emerged as frontrunners in Florida's gubernatorial primary race as the August 18 primary approaches. Donalds holds a commanding lead in Republican polling and fundraising, while Jolly has consolidated Democratic support, though both face scrutiny in the closing weeks.

Lt. Gov. Jay Collins used a Thursday campaign call to position himself as the strongest Republican alternative to Donalds, despite trailing significantly in all metrics. Collins defended his support for Immigration and Customs Enforcement and law enforcement, rejected claims of tension between his campaign and staff inside the governor's office, and urged former Florida House Speaker Paul Renner to leave the race. Collins also argued Donalds could struggle in a general election. "This is a two-person race in the primary," Collins said. "It is between Byron Donalds and myself, and we absolutely have a clear path to do this." A Tyson Group survey released this week placed Donalds at 48 percent, followed by Collins at 9 percent, businessman James Fishback at 8 percent and Renner at 4 percent. About 26 percent of respondents remained undecided. Donalds has raised more than $90 million across his campaign operation and holds President Donald Trump's endorsement. Gov. Ron DeSantis, who appointed Collins lieutenant governor in August 2025, has remained publicly neutral in the primary.

Fishback faces dual challenges as his campaign comes under fire. The Front Line, a Republican group aligned with U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz, announced a $400,000 campaign targeting Fishback over statements the group characterizes as antisemitic. The artificial intelligence-generated ad depicts Fishback as a talking fish making racist comments. Fishback denies being antisemitic and says the spending shows Republican establishment figures are concerned about his campaign. Collins is also challenging Fishback's candidacy in court, alleging Fishback lived and voted in Washington, D.C., and does not meet Florida's seven-year residency requirement for governors. A two-day hearing is scheduled to begin July 21 in Tallahassaba. Fishback says he was born and raised in Florida, has lived in the state throughout his life and purchased a Washington condo only to visit his parents. Because ballots have already been printed, the judge said a ruling against Fishback would likely involve directing election officials not to count votes cast for him rather than removing his name from ballots.

Jolly moved this week to address his past business and political relationship with Clearwater financier Leo Govoni. Federal prosecutors allege Govoni and accountant John Witeck stole more than $100 million from a nonprofit that managed trust funds for people with disabilities. The indictment alleges the scheme operated from 2009 through 2025. Jolly is not a defendant in the case. Jolly previously worked as a vice president at Boston Finance Group, a Govoni-controlled company, before entering Congress. Govoni also supported Jolly's past political campaigns and served as a finance co-chairman during Jolly's unsuccessful 2016 U.S. Senate campaign. In a campaign video, Jolly said he had no knowledge of the alleged theft and welcomed scrutiny of his record. "Unlike too many politicians today who hide behind lawyers or refuse to answer questions, I'm an open book," Jolly said. "Because when you've done nothing wrong, you have nothing to hide."

cards.headline: Florida Fentanyl Summit in Orlando Draws Teens, Grieving Parents and DEA Chief
cards.teaser: Students from anti-drug coalitions across the country joined federal law enforcement at a Florida summit this week to address the ongoing fentanyl crisis.
cards.body:
The Fentanyl Free America Summit in Orlando this week brought together teens from anti-drug coalitions across the country, grieving parents and federal law enforcement officials. Students traveled to Florida to learn about the resurgence of fentanyl so they can return home with a message about one of the country's deadliest drug threats. Hannah Kahn, 18, and Jasmine Figueroa, 19, are members of their community anti-drug coalitions. Figueroa said she has a relative who is addicted to methamphetamine, and seeing how that has destroyed his life has encouraged her to prevent that from happening to anybody else. Figueroa also emphasized that fentanyl is often not known because it is laced within other drugs that people are seeking.

This year's summit welcomed the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration as a partner. DEA Administrator Terrance Cole spent time with victim families and discussed the ongoing threat. Cole said the poison is being manufactured and distributed out of Mexico by the Mexican cartels. He pointed to new tools from the current administration, noting the president has designated Mexican cartels as foreign terrorists, which opens different avenues for targeting them. Mari Rodriguez's daughter, Imam, died of fentanyl poisoning in 2023. Rodriguez said her daughter made the mistake of buying a Percocet pill that had fentanyl in it, and it took her life. Rodriguez said the fight should have started in 2009, when the first fentanyl was found on streets. Kahn said many people have the stereotype that Narcan is only for responders and EMS, but it should be thought of as a household product, just like Benadryl.

hero.headline: Murray Middle School demolition underway after Hurricane Milton tornado damage in Martin County
hero.body:
Demolition has begun at Murray Middle School in Martin County as part of a major reconstruction effort following tornado damage from Hurricane Milton. The project will rebuild buildings destroyed by the tornadoes and add a new administration building, media center, art lab, and a complete parking lot overhaul. The demolition phase alone costs $3.3 million, with the total project cost not yet finalized. Funding comes from local capital improvement, sales tax, and Public Education Capital Outlay.

Kirstie Gernaine, coordinator of public information and community relations for the Martin County School District, explained the school was already scheduled for significant construction work when the hurricane struck. "Murray Middle School was already slated to get all of this construction work with a new admin area, a new media center and a brand new art lab," said Gernaine. "With Hurricane Milton and those tornadoes destroying the buildings in the back buildings 18, 10, and nine we were able to add these on." The tornado damage led to the destruction of three buildings that have now been incorporated into the planned renovation project.

Students displaced from affected classrooms will continue learning in portable classrooms until construction is complete. The school district has implemented safety measures to protect students during the ongoing construction work. Barriers have been placed around the work zone to keep students away from construction areas. School officials have assured parents that students will remain safe throughout the renovation period despite the active construction on campus.

The Martin County School District hopes to complete the renovations by December 2027. The project represents a significant investment in rebuilding and modernizing the middle school campus following the hurricane damage. The reconstruction effort combines previously scheduled improvements with necessary repairs from the tornado destruction, allowing the district to comprehensively update the campus facilities in one extended construction project.

hero.headline: Port St. Lucie Opens Registration for Free City University Program
hero.teaser:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes
hero.body:
Registration is now open for Port St. Lucie City University, a free nine-session program designed to help residents better understand how their local government operates.

Classes begin Wednesday, Aug. 12, and will be held from **5:30 to 8:30 p.m. in the Council Chambers at Port St. Lucie City Hall**, located at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Participants will learn about City departments, municipal services and the decision-making processes that shape the community. The program also gives residents opportunities to meet City staff, ask questions and gain a closer look at the work involved in operating one of Florida's largest cities.

Residents who complete the course will receive a certificate of completion and may also choose to become a City Ambassador, helping share information about City programs and services throughout the community.

City University is intended to encourage civic engagement while strengthening connections between residents and local government. Since the program began in 2016, more than 600 residents have participated.

**Enrollment is limited to 160 participants.**

Residents who are unable to attend the in-person classes can also access City U on Demand, which offers a more flexible way to learn about Port St. Lucie government and municipal operations.

hero.headline: JetBlue ending direct flights from Vero Beach to JFK Airport in September
hero.teaser: JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December.
hero.body:
JetBlue is ending its direct flights between New York's JFK Airport and Vero Beach Regional Airport, citing low passenger demand for the route that launched in December. The airline announced that service between the two airports will end Sept. 9, just nine months after the route began operating with much fanfare and optimistic passengers. JetBlue said in a statement that demand for this new route has not materialized as the airline had hoped.

JetBlue will continue serving Vero Beach through its Boston route and has not announced whether it plans to add any replacement routes from Vero Beach or if it will adjust frequency on the remaining Boston service. All affected customers will be notified directly by JetBlue and will receive full refunds. Passengers with upcoming reservations on the discontinued route are encouraged to contact JetBlue directly or check their email for rebooking options and refund information.

The JFK-Vero Beach route was seen as a major win for the Treasure Coast when it launched in December 2025, providing direct access to one of the nation's busiest airports and potentially boosting tourism to the area. The inaugural flight brought enthusiastic passengers who called the service a game changer for connecting family and friends between New York and the Treasure Coast. The route's cancellation comes as a disappointment to local officials and residents who had hoped the direct connection would strengthen ties between the two regions.

The discontinuation of the JFK route after such a short period highlights the challenges smaller regional airports face in sustaining air service to major hubs. While JetBlue's Boston service will continue to provide some connectivity for Vero Beach travelers, the loss of direct access to JFK eliminates what many saw as a crucial link to the New York metropolitan area. The airline has not indicated whether it might reconsider the route in the future or explore other destinations from Vero Beach Regional Airport.
